title: Income Inequality Before and After Taxes
text:
The Gini coefficient measures income inequality from 0 to 1, with higher values representing greater inequality. This analysis examines which countries experience the largest reduction in inequality after taxes and government benefits.
The data come from the TidyTuesday Income Inequality dataset.

library(tidyverse)

income_inequality <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2025/2025-08-05/income_inequality_processed.csv"
)

section: Which countries reduce inequality the most?
text:
Which countries reduce inequality the most?

ggplot(
  large_reductions,
  aes(
    x = inequality_reduction,
    y = Entity
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#2C7FB8") +
  labs(
    title = "Countries with large reductions in income inequality",
    subtitle = "Difference between pre-tax and post-tax Gini coefficients",
    x = "Reduction in Gini coefficient",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Source: Our World in Data via TidyTuesday"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()








The graph shows countries whose pre-tax Gini coefficient is at least 0.18 higher than their post-tax Gini coefficient, using each country’s most recent available observation. A larger difference indicates that taxes and government benefits are associated with a greater reduction in measured income inequality.
